etymologies.etymologyHTML: From critic +‎ -ism.

definitions.definition: (uncountable) The act of criticising; a critical judgment passed or expressed

quote.citation: 2019 September 3, David Karpf, “Bret Stephens Compared Me to a Nazi Propagandist in the New York Times. It Proved My Point.”, in Esquire‎[1]:
quote.text: Bret Stephens believed that, by virtue of his comfortable position at the New York Times, he ought to be immune from insult or criticism.

definitions.definition: (countable) A critical observation or detailed examination and review.

quote.citation: 1874, Thomas Hardy, Far From the Madding Crowd, Barnes & Noble Classics (2005 publication of 1912 Wessex edition), page 276:
quote.text: Her attitude was that of a person who listens, either to the external world of sound, or to the discourse of thought. A close criticism might have detected signs proving that she was intent on the latter alternative.
